title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is a case of alleged sextortion carried out with synthetic media, in which AI-generated explicit video was used as the leverage in an extortion demand rather than as a product or service. The reported sequence is a fake social media profile, a recorded video call, and then a demand for money backed by the threat of circulating both the recording and AI-made obscene videos. The AI element sits at the point of manufacturing additional compromising material, not at the point of first contact.

The failure mode here is impersonation paired with fabricated media: a false identity used to draw the victim into a call, and generated video used to make the threat credible and repeatable. Nothing in the reporting describes a deployed AI system with safeguards that failed, so this is not a case of a model asserting false facts or of a system running without a human check. It is a case of generative tools being repurposed for coercion, which is a criminal use rather than a deployment failure.

Catching this kind of operation depends on the ordinary investigative trail rather than on model-level detection: the victim's report to the cybercrime team, the phone number already linked to dozens of complaints on the NCRB portal, and the devices and bank accounts that followed. The reporting does not establish how the AI videos were produced, which tools were used, or whether any platform detected and removed the fake profile before the extortion. The arrests are arrests, the FIR is an allegation, and no finding of guilt has been recorded.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student named Md Faisal and three associates from Muzaffarnagar were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI using AI-generated explicit videos. The gang created a fake Facebook profile, recorded the victim during a video call on September 10, then demanded $50,000, about Rs 4.7 crore, threatening to circulate the footage and AI-made obscene videos. The victim reported the matter to the cybercrime team on September 17, and police found the accused's number linked to 40 fraud complaints on the NCRB portal.

Police said the gang had been active since 2023 and cheated hundreds of people in India and abroad. Their phones revealed links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore, and AI sextortion videos were found on their devices. Four members were arrested on Friday, while some associates, including Maroof, remain absconding. An FIR was registered under the BNS and IT Act, and further investigation is ongoing.
